item: Gate G22, "Upgrade and failure acceptance" (supported-driver upgrades, mixed-version compatibility/rejection, outage startup, durable restart, promotion, partition/rejoin, against the final built artifacts)
summary:
Inline citations are relative to /home/vercel-sandbox/kudurru. G22 is still one open row with no evidence section of its own (dev-docs/milestones/v0.2/gaps.md:111, completion-plan.md:221, followup-audit.md:319); everything recorded so far is per-feature. Nothing was executed in this read-only pass, so every finding below comes from reading code and recorded evidence.

- **SQLite upgrade:** the current schema is 9 (internal/store/store.go:27; steps in internal/store/sqlite/schema.go:36-46) and v0.1.0 shipped schema 1 (git tag v0.1.0, same file). Upgrade is one transaction and a newer file is refused (schema.go:142-145; cmd/kudurru/serve.go:184-185, 230-231, 395). Every migration test builds the "old" database with the current code (`migrate(ctx, db, migrations[:N], N, ...)`, e.g. replication_migration_test.go:26). No test opens a file written by the v0.1.0 binary, there is no golden fixture, and no serve-level or built-binary upgrade/downgrade test exists.
- **Kubernetes upgrade:** CRDs stay `v1alpha1` with unchanged scopes and no conversion; five CRDs are new and existing ones are tightened (deploy/kustomize/crd/bases/kudurru.io_dnszones.yaml:506-509, kudurru.io_policies.yaml:195). No test installs v0.1.0 CRDs/objects and upgrades them, and hack/kind-e2e.sh installs only the current charts (lines 358, 383).
- **Unverified upgrade hazard:** SQLite validates every stored public object against the current CRD schema when building the complete image (internal/store/sqlite/replication.go:39, internal/servingbuild/schema.go:103), and one failure fails the whole image (internal/store/replication/codec.go:310-313, internal/servingbuild/prepare.go:106-109). v0.1.0 admitted placeholder `secondary`/`stub` zones and free-form policy rewrites that v0.2 now rejects. The tracker does not mention this.
- **Mixed-version rejection:** implemented and tested in-process only (exact `StoreSchemaVersion` plus required features, codec.go:226-258).
- **Failure acceptance:** the strongest area. SQLite enrolled and static scenarios pass as separate processes (.context/object-forward-20261109/process03.json, four passes at e6a9586b). Kubernetes cold start, outage and lease loss pass in-process on envtest (.context/kube-update-20261110/root-race01.json at HEAD 33ee04bc, 173 passes, no skips).
- **Final artifacts:** only the ordinary e2e tests honor `KUDURRU_E2E_BINARY` (internal/testutil/kudurrutest/kudurrutest.go:35-36, 86-90). Every licensed multi-node harness rebuilds with `-tags licensetest` (test/e2e/auditfixture_test.go:12-24, hack/kind-e2e.sh:313-317, hack/compose-e2e.sh:255-259).
- **Operator docs:** each explicit-action migration has its own page, but CHANGELOG `[0.2.0]` has no upgrade-notes section (v0.1.0 has one at CHANGELOG.md:745) and the rollback sentence at docs/deploy/runbooks.md:390-393 contradicts internal/store/localdb/localdb.go:209-217.
alreadyDone: Newer-schema (downgrade) refusal on every local store, at store level: state.db `TestSchemaNewerThanBinaryRefusesToStart` (internal/store/sqlite/sqlite_test.go:149; also checks the file is untouched and the lock released); local.db `TestSchemaVersioning` (internal/store/localdb/localdb_test.go:124) and `TestLayoutMigration` (blob_test.go:70); querylog.db refusal in internal/querylog/sqlitelog/schema.go:273-275; audit spool `TestSchemaTooNew` (internal/audit/spool/spool_test.go:117); serve maps each to an operator message (cmd/kudurru/serve.go:184-185, 230-231, 395).

SQLite per-step migrations 1 through 9 with rollback and old-binary refusal, on emulated old schemas: `TestMigrationFramework`/`TestMigrationsCoverSchemaVersion` (sqlite_test.go:182,193), `TestMigration2PreservesLegacyObjectsAndStatus` (replication_migration_test.go:19, raw schema-1 rows opened at current schema), `TestCredentialMigration*` (credential_migration_test.go:65,123,173), `TestPrincipalStateMigration*`, `TestPublicIAMMigration*` (iam_migration_test.go:15,76), `TestAuditLegacyUpgradeRestartPrune` (audit_at_rest_test.go:161, pins a fixed legacy hash and the v1/v2 chain boundary), `TestTrustAnchorMigration*`/`TestTrustAnchorUpgrade*`, `TestAnchorRuntimeSchema7UpgradePreservesOriginalRows`, `TestEnrollmentSchema9MigrationPreservesRowsAndRefusesDowngrade` (enrollment_migration_test.go:30). Latest full SQLite default race: 748 passes, no failures or skips, 6m22s (.context/conflict-resolution-20261109/sqlite-race01.json, recorded with the D360/D361 commits of 2026-11-09 07:12Z, 6c86f581).

Auxiliary store migrations: querylog.db 1 to 3 (`TestUpgradeFromSchema1` internal/querylog/sqlitelog/policy_test.go:113, `TestDomainHourMigrationRollbackPrivacy` domain_hour_test.go:72; v0.1.0 shipped querylog schema 2); central PostgreSQL 3 to 6 with compat gating (`TestMigrateConcurrent`, `TestNewerSchema` internal/central/central_test.go:65,97; `TestDictionaryMigration`, `TestDomainHourMigrationPreservesInputGates`, `TestSourceMigrationPreservesOpaqueHistoryAndRefusesOldWriter`); DHCP lease database (`TestLeaseSetupReadOnlyAndV2Migration`, `TestDNSClaimSchemaMigrationRollback`). Latest pass: .context/kube-update-20261110/root-race01.json on HEAD 33ee04bc (173 passes, no skips, 430.7 s) and .context/kube-grant-floors-20261109/root-race01.json at f8dd33d3 (100 passes, no skips).

Kubernetes IAM offline migration from private Secrets to public objects, with crash and resume coverage on envtest using the production CRDs: internal/iammigrate (`TestEnvtestFullCutoverAndPrivateBindings`, `TestEnvtestEveryWriteCrashAndRollbackArtifacts`, `TestEnvtestUIDLessLegacyTokenStrictFloor`, others), CLI (cmd/kudurru/iam_migrate_test.go:42,64,109), runtime gate (`TestServeAuthMigrationGateCoversPublicAndAuthenticatedRoutes`, serve_iam_gate_test.go:32). The source Secrets are test-constructed, not written by a v0.1.0 binary.

F73 AuditLog legacy HMAC cutover is implemented and tested (`TestAuditKeysCLIExplicitLegacyImport` cmd/kudurru/audit_keys_test.go:63; `TestLegacyExplicitCutoffAndNoDowngrade` internal/audit/auditkeys/ring_test.go:140) and documented (docs/deploy/runbooks.md:273-364, docs/deploy/helm.md:40-49).

Operator documentation exists for each migration that needs explicit action, just not in one place: Kubernetes IAM offline migration (docs/deploy/iam-upgrade.md), AuditLog key provisioning (runbooks.md:273-364), F01 cluster-ID pin with an upgrade-compatibility paragraph (runbooks.md:85-119), separate SQLite storage offline move (docs/deploy/sqlite-storage.md), central schema 4/5/6 and mixed versions (docs/deploy/postgres.md:184-229), release-namespace defaults (helm.md:446-470), generic upgrade procedure (runbooks.md:366-405), static twins (docs/deploy/compose-ha.md), enrolled join (docs/deploy/sqlite-join.md).

Last recorded hosted kind pass is rerun attempt 2 on ffd18d41 (completion-plan.md:1766-1767); last fully green hosted CI is 42553837447 on 9963dec2 (gaps.md:6734). remaining.title: Record the G22 scope decisions in the decision log
remaining.detail:
Add decisions after D366 in dev-docs/design-record.md section 16 and reference them from the G22 rows.

1. Final built artifact: the CGO-disabled `make build` binary and the Dockerfile image built from the final head with release flags. Licensed multi-node scenarios run on the same source plus `-tags licensetest`, which only adds one trusted public key (internal/license/testkey.go:1-19, keyring.go:21-36). Precedent: hack/kind-e2e.sh:313-317, hack/compose-e2e.sh:255-259, test/e2e/auditfixture_test.go:12-15.
2. Upgrade baseline: v0.1.0 (tag 89c59f89; state.db schema 1, querylog.db 2, central 3, local.db layout 2) is the only supported source release. Fixtures must be written by a v0.1.0 binary, not emulated with current code.
3. Mixed-version policy: schema 9 is the first enrollment-capable schema, so no older enrolled peer exists in the field. Refusal rests on exact `StoreSchemaVersion` and required features (internal/store/replication/codec.go:226-258). Kubernetes v0.1 to v0.2 is an offline upgrade whenever private IAM Secrets or HMAC AuditLog batches exist (docs/deploy/iam-upgrade.md:14-18, runbooks.md:296-300); otherwise rolling.
4. Handling of legacy stored objects that the tightened v0.2 schema rejects (outcome of G22-WP2).
remaining.acceptance: completion-plan.md:226 (G25: plan, audit, ledger and changelog consistent) and gaps.md:111 ("against the final built artifacts" needs a definition before a pass can be claimed). Proof: the new D-rows exist and are cited by the G22 evidence section; the decision table still passes whatever docs checks `make test` runs.

remaining.title: Upgrade a data directory written by the released v0.1.0 binary, and refuse downgrade, at the built-binary level (SQLite)
remaining.detail:
Missing today: any test that opens files written by v0.1.0, and any process-level check of the upgrade or of the "newer kudurru" refusal.

- Add a helper next to `Build` in internal/testutil/kudurrutest/kudurrutest.go (lines 84-101) that produces the previous release: `git archive v0.1.0 | tar -x -C <tmp>` then `CGO_ENABLED=0 go build -trimpath -o kudurru-v0.1.0 ./cmd/kudurru`. A new `KUDURRU_E2E_PREVIOUS_BINARY` overrides it with a downloaded, checksum-verified release binary.
- New test/e2e/upgrade_test.go, `TestUpgradeFromV01DataDirectory`:
  1. Start v0.1.0 (sqlite driver; `serve` passed explicitly because the 0.1.0 image had no default command, CHANGELOG.md:128-131).
  2. Create a primary zone and record sets (objectsDir and API-owned), a BlockList/ClientGroup/Policy, a local user and API token (`admin create-token`), one UI settings change, audit rows and query-log rows. Stop cleanly.
  3. Start the final binary (`kudurruBin`, honoring `KUDURRU_E2E_BINARY`) on the same directory.
  4. Assert: ready; the same UDP/TCP answers; SOA serial not regressed; the old token still authenticates (migrations 3-5); `kudurru audit verify` passes across the v1/v2 chain boundary (migration 6); query rows and ids retained (querylog 2 to 3); state.db `schema_version` equals `store.SchemaVersion`; `Kudurru/default` created once (cmd/kudurru/serving_settings.go:20-42).
  5. Restart twice (idempotent).
  6. Start v0.1.0 on the upgraded directory: non-zero exit, a "newer" message, and `schema_version` rows unchanged.
- `TestBuiltBinaryRefusesNewerDatabases`: bump `schema_version` in state.db, local.db, querylog.db and the audit spool in turn. The final binary must exit non-zero naming the file (serve.go:184-185, 230-231, 395) without modifying it.
- Commit a small golden `internal/store/sqlite/testdata/v0.1.0/state.db` produced by the same script, with a provenance README, and an in-package `TestOpenReleasedV01Golden` so plain `make test` covers real v0.1 bytes without the tag build.
remaining.acceptance: gaps.md:111 ("Run supported-driver upgrades ... against the final built artifacts"); followup-audit.md:319 ("All supported-driver migrations, durable restarts ... remain final-artifact gates"); dev-docs/milestones/v0.2/README.md:383 (V2-IAM: "Verify upgrade from existing Secrets/SQLite identities ... revocation across restarts"); followup-audit.md:67 (F02d: re-run snapshot/private-state migration acceptance on final drivers). Proof: `KUDURRU_E2E=1 KUDURRU_E2E_BINARY=$PWD/bin/kudurru go test -race -count=1 ./test/e2e -run 'TestUpgradeFromV01DataDirectory|TestBuiltBinaryRefusesNewerDatabases'` and `go test -race ./internal/store/sqlite -run TestOpenReleasedV01Golden` pass with zero skips.

remaining.title: Prove and fix behavior for v0.1 objects that the tightened v0.2 schema rejects
remaining.detail:
v0.1.0 CRDs admitted shapes reserved for v0.2:
- `DNSZone.spec.type: secondary|stub` with no `secondary`/`stub` block (v0.1.0 kudurru.io_dnszones.yaml:429-437; its only spec rule was the fallback rule at 453-455).
- Unconstrained `Policy.spec.rewrites[]` items.

v0.2 adds `self.type != 'secondary' || has(self.secondary)` and the stub equivalent (api/v1alpha1/dnszone_types.go:230-231; deploy/kustomize/crd/bases/kudurru.io_dnszones.yaml:506-509), plus a rewrite enum, either-or rule and bounds (kudurru.io_policies.yaml:162-201).

On SQLite, every stored public object passes through `ValidateStored` with the current schema when the complete image is validated (internal/store/sqlite/replication.go:39; internal/servingbuild/schema.go:103). The first failure returns from `Validate` (internal/store/replication/codec.go:310-313) and fails `PrepareImage` for the whole image (internal/servingbuild/prepare.go:106-109). After an upgrade, one such legacy object could therefore stop all publication. This is unverified by execution; the tracker does not mention it.

Step 1, failing-first tests:
- internal/store/sqlite: seed raw schema-1 rows as `insertLegacyCredential` does (credential_migration_test.go:38-56) for a placeholder secondary zone and a placeholder rewrite, open at the current schema, call `ValidateImage`.
- cmd/kudurru: a mounted `runServe` test on that directory asserting DNS and readiness.

Step 2, choose and record the handling (see designOptions). Recommended: validate all public objects inside the `migrate` transaction, next to `validateAuditFormats` (internal/store/sqlite/schema.go:177-181). Refuse the upgrade with an error naming kind, name and rule, leaving the database at its old version. Precedent: `TestPublicIAMMigrationRollsBackInvalidObjects` (iam_migration_test.go:76).

Step 3: add a table test in internal/store/validator proving every v0.1.0 sample (v0.1.0 deploy/kustomize/samples/*.yaml) still validates, and that BlockLists carrying the v0.1-defaulted `refreshInterval: 24h` remain valid (the default was removed from kudurru.io_blocklists.yaml).
remaining.acceptance: gaps.md:111 (supported-driver upgrades); README.md:376 (V2-ZONE: "restart recovery, and last-good data") and README.md:364-366 ("last-good snapshots during outages"); gaps.md:108 (G21: no unexplained 503 in supported workflows). Proof: new `TestUpgradeLegacyPlaceholderObjects*` (sqlite), `TestRunServeSQLiteUpgradeWithLegacyPlaceholders` (cmd/kudurru) and `TestV01SamplesRemainValid` (validator) pass; behavior is recorded as a D-number and in the upgrade notes.

remaining.title: Kubernetes upgrade acceptance from v0.1.0 CRDs, stored objects and chart
remaining.detail:
Missing today: any test where objects admitted under v0.1.0 CRDs are read, updated and served after the v0.2 CRDs replace them, and any Helm upgrade-path check.

- Fixtures: copy `git show v0.1.0:deploy/kustomize/crd/{bases,audit,dhcp}/*.yaml` and `deploy/kustomize/samples/*.yaml` into internal/store/kube/testdata/v0.1.0/ with a provenance note.
- envtest test `TestEnvtestCRDUpgradeFromV01` (internal/store/kube, harness at envtest_test.go:51): install v0.1 CRDs; create the samples with status, objects in `default` (the pre-release-namespace layout, docs/deploy/helm.md:461-466) and legacy private IAM Secrets; update the CRDs to the current bases. Assert Established, `status.storedVersions == [v1alpha1]`, every object readable through the v0.2 kube store, `UpdateStatus` works, an unchanged-spec write works (ratcheting), a write using a new v0.2 field works, and the resulting local.db snapshot cold-starts.
- Process variant in test/e2e, modeled on kubeaudit_test.go:35-60: the v0.1.0 binary writes with the kube driver; CRDs are upgraded; `kudurru iam migrate status|plan|begin --offline` runs (docs/deploy/iam-upgrade.md:43-50); `kudurru audit keys init --legacy-master-file ... --legacy-before ...` runs (runbooks.md:313-317); the final binary serves the same answers, the old token authenticates and `audit verify` accepts the legacy batches.
- Helm: a deploy/ test comparing a committed `helm template` render of the v0.1.0 chart with the current chart (default and HA values) and asserting immutable fields are unchanged: workload `spec.selector`, StatefulSet `volumeClaimTemplates`, Service and Secret names.
- Optional `UPGRADE_FROM=0.1.0` phase in hack/kind-e2e.sh: install the published 0.1.0 charts, upgrade the CRD chart then the chart under dig load (runbooks.md:375-388). Needs ghcr.io pulls.
remaining.acceptance: gaps.md:111; gaps.md:86 (G12: "Validate migration, revocation, scoped grants, restart ... for every supported route"); README.md:383 ("Verify upgrade from existing Secrets/SQLite identities"); completion-plan.md:206 (F73 "explicit upgrade provisioning required"); completion-plan.md:80 (F01). Proof: `KUBEBUILDER_ASSETS=$PWD/bin/k8s/1.37.0-linux-amd64 go test -race -count=1 ./internal/store/kube -run TestEnvtestCRDUpgradeFromV01`, the e2e process test, and `go test ./deploy -run 'Upgrade|Immutable'` pass with zero skips.

remaining.title: Kubernetes outage cold start, restart and Lease handoff with built binaries (process level)
remaining.detail:
The Kubernetes failure scenarios pass only in-process (`runServe` inside the test binary: cmd/kudurru/serve_offline_test.go:31, externaldns_crd_failover_test.go:100). The only kube-driver process test is `TestKubeAuditAcrossReplicas` (test/e2e/kubeaudit_test.go:35), which covers audit history and empty-directory restart.

Add test/e2e `TestKubeProcessesColdStartLeaseLossAndRejoin`: two built binaries with the kube driver on envtest, each reaching the API server through its own TCP relay (reuse `enrolledRelay`, enrolled_cluster_test.go:29-110), with `store.kube.expectedClusterID` pinned.

1. API server unreachable at start with a fresh matching local.db: UDP/TCP answers and the readiness/`snapshotAge` contract (F64b).
2. Missing or foreign pin, or an identity-free old snapshot: SERVFAIL and unready (the matrix at serve_offline_test.go:41-46).
3. Partition the Lease holder: the other acquires `kudurru-controller`, the partitioned node keeps last-good answers, and after healing there is one leader and converged data.
4. Stop and restart both on existing directories and on empty ones: resync without loss.

Use the licensed fixture only where two replicas must write.
remaining.acceptance: gaps.md:111 ("outage startup, durable restart, promotion and partition/rejoin against the final built artifacts"); followup-audit.md:63 (F01); gaps.md:85 (G11: "primary loss and restart while DNS continues from valid local data"). Proof: `KUDURRU_E2E=1 KUBEBUILDER_ASSETS=... go test -race -count=1 ./test/e2e -run TestKubeProcessesColdStartLeaseLossAndRejoin` passes three consecutive times with zero skips.

remaining.title: Mixed-version process acceptance with the released v0.1.0 binary
remaining.detail:
Rejection is unit-tested, but no test runs two different releases side by side. Using the v0.1.0 binary from G22-WP1:

- (a) Legacy internal listener during a host-by-host Compose HA upgrade (docs/deploy/compose-ha.md:112-116). One v0.1.0 node and one final node share `KUDURRU_ENCRYPTION_KEY`; the final node uses `cluster.role: static` with the old node as a peer. Assert the final node's `/nodes` reports the old peer's version and readiness or an explicit error (never a crash or a silent "ready"), status and list bodies by digest work both ways, absent `/internal/catalogue` and `/internal/zones` are treated as unsupported (internalapi/catalogue.go:38, zones.go:46), and the old node never receives member-enrollment routes (D342 SNI split).
- (b) Central PostgreSQL. A v0.1.0 node is attached; the final node migrates 3 to 6 with compat 6 (internal/central/migrate.go:21-23). Assert the old node reports `CentralIncompatible`, keeps answering DNS and keeps its local spool; after its binary is replaced, its backlog ships once (docs/deploy/postgres.md:184-229). Needs Docker PostgreSQL as in `make test-postgres` (Makefile:99-106).
- (c) Enrolled members. Assert a v0.1.0 binary pointed at an enrolled schema-9 directory refuses to start. In-process schema/feature refusals remain the evidence for enrolled peers (per the G22-WP0 decision).
- (d) Edge supervisor skew. Keep the RC.4 status fallback (internal/api/edge.go:90-96) covered and run `make edge-check` in the final pass.
remaining.acceptance: gaps.md:111 ("mixed-version compatibility/rejection"); README.md:382 (V2-HA: "stale/wrong-cluster/newer-schema snapshots"); design-record.md:1603 (D11: follower halts on version skew). Proof: new `TestMixedVersionStaticPeerV01`, `TestMixedVersionCentralDatabaseV01` and `TestV01BinaryRefusesEnrolledDirectory` in test/e2e pass with zero skips (`KUDURRU_REQUIRE_POSTGRES=1`).

remaining.title: Make the harnesses run on prebuilt final artifacts and remove silent skips
remaining.detail:
- test/e2e/auditfixture_test.go:16-33 runs `go build -tags=licensetest` inside every licensed test (six rebuilds per run) and ignores `KUDURRU_E2E_BINARY`. Accept `KUDURRU_E2E_LICENSED_BINARY` (prebuilt with the release ldflags plus the tag) and log `kudurru version` of every binary used, so the evidence names the artifact.
- hack/kind-e2e.sh:312-317 always builds its image. Honor `BUILD=0` with a supplied `IMAGE`, as hack/compose-e2e.sh:35-39, 253-264 already does.
- .github/workflows/ci.yml e2e job (lines 290-318) has no envtest install step, so `TestKubeAuditAcrossReplicas` appears to skip there (test/e2e/kubeaudit_test.go:41-44). Add the envtest cache/install steps used by the go-test job (ci.yml:93-102) and a `KUDURRU_REQUIRE_ENVTEST=1` switch that fails instead of skipping, mirroring `KUDURRU_REQUIRE_IAM_ENVTEST` (internal/iammigrate/envtest_test.go:44-47).
- Optional `make g22` target chaining the runbook in G22-WP8 and writing JSON evidence under .context/.

remaining.title: Consolidated 0.1.x to 0.2.0 upgrade notes and runbook corrections
remaining.detail:
1. Add "Installation and upgrade notes" to CHANGELOG.md `[0.2.0]` (the 0.1.0 section has one at line 745) and an "Upgrading from 0.1.x" subsection under docs/deploy/runbooks.md:366. It should list, in order:
   - Back up; downgrade is unsupported once started (state.db 1 to 9, querylog.db 2 to 3, local.db marker 1 to 9).
   - Upgrade `kudurru-crds` first: five new CRDs (Kudurru, IdentityProvider, Integration, RoleBinding, ServiceAccount).
   - Kubernetes with private IAM Secrets: offline `kudurru iam migrate` (docs/deploy/iam-upgrade.md). That page is currently linked only from docs/architecture/access.md:949 and docs/deploy/rolebindings.md:59, not from runbooks.md, helm.md or docs/deploy/README.md.
   - AuditLog key provisioning and legacy cutover before `audit.store: auditlog` resumes (runbooks.md:273-364).

recommendation:
G22 is mostly a qualification gate, but two things are real work rather than re-running tests: nothing proves an upgrade from bytes written by the released v0.1.0 binary on either driver, and legacy objects that the tightened v0.2 schema rejects may stop SQLite publication after upgrade.

**Order of work**
1. **G22-WP0, decisions.** Record the artifact definition, the v0.1.0 baseline and the mixed-version policy. This follows D11 (design-record.md:1603: schema version in every driver, newer-on-disk refuses, follower halts on skew), the licensetest precedent the kind and compose checks already use, and the D353/D358 pattern of stating deferred limits explicitly.
2. **G22-WP6, harness switches (S).** Lets every later run name the exact binary and removes the hosted envtest skip.
3. **G22-WP1 and G22-WP2, SQLite.** Build the v0.1.0 binary from the local git tag, write a real data directory, upgrade it with the final binary, and settle the legacy-object question first: it is the only item here that could be a product defect, and it changes the upgrade notes.
4. **G22-WP3 and G22-WP4, Kubernetes.** v0.1.0 CRD and object upgrade on envtest, plus process-level cold start and Lease handoff using the existing relay and kubeaudit patterns. This avoids a hard dependency on kind and published images.
5. **G22-WP5, mixed-version process checks,** then **G22-WP7, docs.**
6. **G22-WP8, the single final pass** on the final head with zero skips.

**Why this fixture approach**
I would combine building v0.1.0 from the tag at e2e time with one small committed golden state.db. The tag build exercises the real old binary on both drivers and for mixed-version checks; the golden file keeps plain `make test` and hosted CI covering real v0.1 bytes without network or a second build.

**Legacy objects**
For G22-WP2 I recommend refusing the migration transactionally with a named-object error, following the migratePublicIAM rollback precedent (internal/store/sqlite/iam_migration_test.go:76) and D326's "never repair" rule for current-schema corruption. The alternatives silently change serving or weaken the D75 parity between Docker and Kubernetes validation.

**Owner involvement**
Nothing in G22 needs the owner. G22-WP9 is optional and only applies if the strict reading of "final built artifacts" is wanted for licensed scenarios. AD (D353), independent-VM keepalived (D358), F64c and release publication stay out of scope.

designOptions.name: A. Released binary built from the v0.1.0 tag at test time, plus one committed golden state.db (recommended)
designOptions.description: `kudurrutest` gains a previous-release build (`git archive v0.1.0`, `go build`) with a `KUDURRU_E2E_PREVIOUS_BINARY` override. e2e tests write real v0.1 state on SQLite and on envtest Kubernetes, then upgrade with the final binary. A small golden state.db produced by the same script is committed for in-package tests.
designOptions.pros: Uses real bytes from the real old binary on both drivers, and the same binary serves mixed-version and downgrade-refusal checks. Needs no published images or network beyond the Go module cache. The fixture can be regenerated by script. The golden file keeps `make test` and hosted CI covering v0.1 without the extra build.
designOptions.cons: Building the tag needs the v0.1.0 module dependencies (possibly a download) and one to two minutes of build time. A binary fixture is added to the repository. A tag build is not byte-identical to the published ko/goreleaser artifact unless the override points at a verified release download.

designOptions.name: B. Committed golden fixtures only
designOptions.description: Generate the state.db, querylog.db and local.db files and the v0.1 CRD/object YAML once, commit them, and test upgrades purely from those files.
designOptions.pros: Fast, hermetic, and runs in every `go test`. No second binary to build.
designOptions.cons: No mixed-version or built-binary downgrade check. Fixtures go stale silently and cannot exercise v0.1 runtime behavior (internal listener, central shipping, old Lease holder). Kubernetes Secrets and AuditLog batches still need a live writer to be realistic.

designOptions.name: C. Container-level upgrade in kind and Compose from published 0.1.0 images and charts
designOptions.description: Add an `UPGRADE_FROM=0.1.0` phase to hack/kind-e2e.sh and hack/compose-e2e.sh that installs the published release, then upgrades the CRD chart, the chart and the images under dig load.
designOptions.pros: Closest to what an operator does. Exercises Helm immutability, the rolling Deployment and preStop lameduck, and real volumes.
designOptions.cons: Needs ghcr.io pulls and kind (not installed here; hosted kind downloads have returned 504, completion-plan.md:1694-1699). Slow and harder to debug. The licensed three-replica target image still needs licensetest trust, and the 0.1.0 image cannot trust the test key at all, so the source side is limited to unlicensed behavior. Best as an optional addition to A, not the gate.

designOptions.name: Legacy invalid objects: refuse the migration, quarantine, or tolerate
designOptions.description: Three ways to handle v0.1 objects that v0.2 CRD rules reject on SQLite: (1) validate inside the migration transaction and refuse the upgrade with a named error; (2) migrate but exclude those objects from the complete image with a NotReady condition; (3) run stored validation in a ratcheting mode that tolerates them.
designOptions.pros: (1) is atomic, explicit and matches existing migration precedent; the operator fixes the object with the old binary and retries. (2) keeps DNS up for everything else without operator action. (3) is the smallest change.
designOptions.cons: (1) blocks the upgrade until the operator acts and needs a clear doc path. (2) changes complete-image semantics (manifest counts, replication digests) and is the largest change. (3) weakens the rule that Docker rejects exactly what Kubernetes rejects (D75) and lets invalid data reach compilers that now assume the new invariants.

risks: Legacy stored objects may stop SQLite serving after upgrade. Placeholder `secondary`/`stub` zones or free-form policy rewrites admitted by v0.1.0 fail the v0.2 stored validation, and one failing object fails the complete image (internal/store/sqlite/replication.go:39, internal/servingbuild/prepare.go:106-109). Not verified by execution; G22-WP2 must reproduce it before the upgrade notes are written.

No hosted qualification is recorded for HEAD 33ee04bc. The last green hosted CI is 9963dec2 and the last hosted kind pass is a rerun on ffd18d41. Hosted runs have also hit infrastructure 504s (kind and golangci-lint downloads) and one unexplained intermittent failure, `TestRunServeDirectAnchorsBootstrapTransportsRestartAndDisabled` (HTTP/2 INTERNAL_ERROR, later H3_INTERNAL_ERROR; completion-plan.md:1768-1776). Either can block a zero-failure final pass.

The schema can still move. Any remaining v0.2 feature that adds SQLite schema 10, a replication required feature, a central migration or a CRD change invalidates the G22 fixtures and evidence. G22-WP8 must run after every other package is merged.

Licensed multi-node evidence is on licensetest-trust builds, not the byte-identical release artifact. If the owner reads "final built artifacts" strictly, G22-WP9 (a production-signed key) is needed and is outside the sandbox.

Building v0.1.0 from the tag needs its module dependencies (network or a warm module cache) and assumes the Go 1.27.3 toolchain here builds that tag. If not, fall back to a verified download of the published v0.1.0 binary, which needs network access to GitHub releases.

A Kubernetes v0.1 to v0.2 upgrade is effectively offline when private IAM Secrets or HMAC AuditLog batches exist, while the generic runbook describes a rolling Deployment (docs/deploy/runbooks.md:375-388 versus iam-upgrade.md:14-18). Until G22-WP7 lands, operators following only the generic runbook can end up with login refused by the migration gate or audit shipping stopped.

The documented rollback is wrong for persisted local.db (runbooks.md:390-393 versus internal/store/localdb/localdb.go:209-217). There is no automated downgrade path for state.db, IAM objects or audit trust, so a failed upgrade without a backup is unrecoverable by design.

Process-level tests are timing-sensitive on shared CPU. The enrolled scenarios needed a settle fix on 2026-11-09 (dfa01388) and the static test had earlier node-b startup failures (D349). Run the final pass on an otherwise idle machine and keep any failed attempt in the evidence.
kind is not installed locally and the kind script cannot take a prebuilt image until G22-WP6. The Kubernetes container-level part of the pass depends on hosted runners or a local kind install.

Enrolled process children are CGO-disabled and not race-instrumented (completion-plan.md:1633-1635), so data races inside child servers are caught only by the in-process race suites. Both layers are needed for closure.
